Health care expenditure and use of US adults, MEPS panel 23 (2018-2019)

Source: R/data-meps.R
meps.Rd

A real public two-year person panel from the US Medical Expenditure Panel Survey (MEPS) Household Component, longitudinal file HC-217 (panel 23). The unit is a person, the time index is the calendar year (2018, 2019): each of 3,000 adults contributes exactly two rows. Expenditure outcomes have the classic health-economics shape (a mass of zeros plus a long right tail), utilisation outcomes are overdispersed counts with many zeros, and insurance, income and chronic conditions vary over time within person, which makes the data a natural testbed for two-part, hurdle, tobit, gamma, quantile, selection and correlated random effects (Mundlak) panel models.

Usage

meps

Format

A data frame with 6,000 rows (3,000 persons x 2 years) and 20 columns. The panel index pair is c("id", "year").

id

integer person identifier (1-3000), the panel individual index; a new sequential id, not the MEPS DUPERSID

year

integer calendar year (2018 or 2019), the panel time index (MEPS suffix Y1, Y2)

totexp

numeric total health care expenditure in the year, US dollars, all payers (TOTEXPY1, TOTEXPY2); 14 percent zeros

oopexp

numeric out-of-pocket (self or family) expenditure, US dollars (TOTSLFY1, TOTSLFY2); never larger than totexp

anyexp

integer indicator (0/1) of any health care expenditure in the year, as.integer(totexp > 0)

officevis

integer number of office-based provider visits (OBTOTVY1, OBTOTVY2)

ervis

integer number of emergency room visits (ERTOTY1, ERTOTY2)

ipstays

integer number of hospital inpatient discharges (IPDISY1, IPDISY2)

insurance

factor health insurance coverage in the year (INSCOVY1, INSCOVY2): private (any private coverage), public (public coverage only, e.g. Medicare, Medicaid), uninsured (uninsured all year); reference level private

age

integer age in years at the end of the year (or last age in scope), top-coded at 85 (AGEY1X, AGEY2X). Age rises by one year for (almost) everyone, so within person it is collinear with the year: use it in pooled and random effects models but not as a time-varying regressor in within or Mundlak (cre = TRUE) fits

sex

factor male, female (SEX), time-invariant

race

factor race and ethnicity (RACETHX): hispanic, white (non-Hispanic white only), black (non-Hispanic black only), asian (non-Hispanic Asian only), other (non-Hispanic other or multiple race); time-invariant

region

factor Census region at the end of the year (REGIONY1, REGIONY2): northeast, midwest, south, west

povcat

factor family income as a percent of the federal poverty line, in categories (POVCATY1, POVCATY2): poor (below 100 percent, including negative income), nearpoor (100 to below 125), low (125 to below 200), middle (200 to below 400), high (400 or more)

povlev

numeric family income as a percent of the poverty line, one decimal (POVLEVY1, POVLEVY2); can be negative

health

ordered factor self-rated (perceived) health status, excellent < verygood < good < fair < poor, from the interview round closing the year (2018: round 3 RTHLTH3; 2019: round 5 RTHLTH5), as in the MEPS annual files; 4 values NA (refused, don't know or not ascertained)

nchronic

integer number (0-8) of eight MEPS priority conditions ever diagnosed as reported in that year: high blood pressure, coronary heart disease, stroke, emphysema, high cholesterol, diabetes, arthritis, asthma (HIBPDXYt, CHDDXYt, STRKDXYt, EMPHDXYt, CHOLDXYt, DIABDXYt_M18, ARTHDXYt, ASTHDXYt); refused, don't know and inapplicable answers count as not diagnosed. The longitudinal file carries the same "ever diagnosed" answers in both years, so nchronic is constant within person: a baseline morbidity measure, dropped by within (fixed effects) estimators

longwt

numeric MEPS panel 23 longitudinal person weight (LONGWT), constant within person

varstr

integer variance estimation stratum (VARSTR)

varpsu

integer variance estimation primary sampling unit within stratum (VARPSU)

Source

Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ), Medical Expenditure Panel Survey, Household Component, public use file HC-217: MEPS Panel 23 Longitudinal Data File (released December 2021). Rockville, MD: AHRQ. https://meps.ahrq.gov/mepsweb/data_stats/download_data_files_detail.jsp?cboPufNumber=HC-217. Data: https://meps.ahrq.gov/mepsweb/data_files/pufs/h217/h217dta.zip.

MEPS is produced by AHRQ, an agency of the US federal government; the public use files carry no copyright notice. AHRQ "requests that users cite AHRQ and the Medical Expenditure Panel Survey as the data source in any publications or research based upon these data." The files are released under the following Data Use Agreement (section A of the HC-217 documentation, https://meps.ahrq.gov/mepsweb/data_stats/download_data/pufs/h217/h217doc.shtml), which binds every user of this extract as well:

"Individual identifiers have been removed from the micro-data contained in these files. Nevertheless, under sections 308 (d) and 903 (c) of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 242m and 42 U.S.C. 299 a-1), data collected by the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ) and/or the National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS) may not be used for any purpose other than for the purpose for which they were supplied; any effort to determine the identity of any reported cases is prohibited by law. Therefore in accordance with the above referenced Federal Statute, it is understood that: (1) No one is to use the data in this data set in any way except for statistical reporting and analysis; and (2) If the identity of any person or establishment should be discovered inadvertently, then (a) no use will be made of this knowledge, (b) the Director Office of Management AHRQ will be advised of this incident, (c) the information that would identify any individual or establishment will be safeguarded or destroyed, as requested by AHRQ, and (d) no one else will be informed of the discovered identity; and (3) No one will attempt to link this data set with individually identifiable records from any data sets other than the Medical Expenditure Panel Survey or the National Health Interview Survey. By using these data you signify your agreement to comply with the above stated statutorily based requirements with the knowledge that deliberately making a false statement in any matter within the jurisdiction of any department or agency of the Federal Government violates Title 18 part 1 Chapter 47 Section 1001 and is punishable by a fine of up to $10,000 or up to 5 years in prison."

Validation (in data-raw/meps.R): on the full HC-217 file the unweighted codebook frequencies of INSCOVY1, RACETHX, POVCATY2, TOTEXPY1 and OBTOTVY2 are reproduced exactly, and LONGWT sums to 305.7 million over the 13,044 ALL5RDS = 1 persons as in the documentation. The LONGWT-weighted mean total expenditure per person is 5,676 dollars in 2018 and 6,249 dollars in 2019, against 6,063 and 6,252 dollars from the annual files in AHRQ Statistical Briefs #533 and #540; the share with any expense is 87.1 and 84.4 percent against about 87 and 86 percent. The 2018 gap (-6 percent) is expected: the longitudinal weight covers only people in scope for the whole two years, which excludes 2018 decedents, whose end-of-life spending is high.

Details

The extract keeps persons with data for all five interview rounds (ALL5RDS = 1, in scope for the whole of 2018 and 2019) who were aged 18 or older in 2018, and draws a stratified random sample of 3,000 of the 10,084 eligible persons (strata: 2018 age 18-34, 35-49, 50-64, 65+; proportional allocation; set.seed(20261101)). The original person identifier DUPERSID is replaced by a new sequential id so that rows cannot be matched back to the public file or linked to other sources. The build script, with its validation against the codebook and against official AHRQ estimates, is data-raw/meps.R in the package's GitHub repository.

Because the sample is drawn with equal probability within age strata, longwt remains approximately valid for weighted descriptive statistics of the adult population (the 2018 and 2019 weighted means of totexp in the sample are within 2 percent of those of all eligible adults in the full file), but the design variables varstr and varpsu only describe the original MEPS design: design-based standard errors computed from this subsample are approximate. The panglm examples below are unweighted model-based fits, as usual for teaching.

Teaching use

All outcomes are observed for every person in both years, so the data are a balanced short panel (T = 2): within and Mundlak (CRE) estimators are identified only from people whose insurance or income changed between 2018 and 2019 (223 insurance changes, 1,114 income-category changes), and age and nchronic should enter only pooled or random effects fits.

  • Does insurance status change health spending, and through which margin? totexp is zero for 14 percent of person-years and highly skewed: twopart() (probit + gamma, model = "pooling" or "random") with partialeffects() for the dollar effect of being uninsured; compare with panglm(family = "tobit") on log1p(totexp).

  • Is the cross-sectional insurance gap causal or selection? panglm() family = "gamma" on positive spending, model = "pooling" or "random" versus model = "within" (identified from people who gained or lost coverage).

  • Who uses any care? anyexp with family = "probit", model = "random", cre = TRUE (Mundlak test of the random effects assumption) and partialeffects().

  • Utilisation counts. officevis (overdispersed, 24 percent zeros) or ervis, ipstays (mostly zero) with family = "negbin" or "poisson", model = "random" or "within"; panhurdle() for the zero versus positive split with fixed effects.

  • Distributional effects. panqr() (model = "canay" or "pooling") on log1p(totexp) or log(oopexp + 1) at several quantiles; model = "mmqr" needs T >= 3 and does not apply here.

  • Selection on spending. panselect() with anyexp as the selection equation and log spending as the outcome (the alternative to the two-part model); self-rated health as an ordered outcome with family = "oprobit", model = "random".

Statistical Brief #540. Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality, Rockville, MD. https://meps.ahrq.gov/data_files/publications/st540/stat540.shtml

Cohen, J. W., Cohen, S. B. and Banthin, J. S. (2009). The Medical Expenditure Panel Survey: a national information resource to support healthcare cost research and inform policy and practice. Medical Care, 47(7 Suppl 1), S44-S50. doi:10.1097/MLR.0b013e3181a23e3a

data(meps)
str(meps)

# survey-weighted mean spending per adult and share with any expense
sapply(split(meps, meps$year), function(d)
  c(mean = weighted.mean(d$totexp, d$longwt),
    anyexp = weighted.mean(d$anyexp, d$longwt)))
#>               2018         2019
#> mean   6566.098685 7490.9550582
#> anyexp    0.866528    0.8375669

# two-part model: P(any spending) and E(spending | spending > 0)
tp <- twopart(totexp ~ insurance + I(age / 10) + sex + nchronic + povcat,
              data = meps, index = c("id", "year"), positive = "gamma")
summary(tp)

# positive spending: pooled versus within (coverage switchers)
pos <- subset(meps, totexp > 0)
fe <- panglm(totexp ~ insurance + povcat, data = pos,
             index = c("id", "year"), family = "gamma", model = "within")
summary(fe)

# any use: correlated random effects probit with Mundlak test

              index = c("id", "year"), family = "probit",
              model = "random", cre = TRUE)

# censored log spending: tobit
summary(panglm(log1p(totexp) ~ insurance + I(age / 10) + sex + nchronic,
               data = meps, index = c("id", "year"), family = "tobit",
               model = "pooling"))

# quantiles of log spending with individual effects (the many tied
# values of log1p(totexp) make quantreg warn that the solution may be
# nonunique)
qr <- suppressWarnings(panqr(log1p(totexp) ~ insurance + povlev,
  data = meps, index = c("id", "year"), tau = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75),
  model = "canay", boot = 50, seed = 1))
summary(qr)

# selection correction for log spending observed only if positive
meps$logexp <- ifelse(meps$totexp > 0, log(meps$totexp), NA)
summary(panselect(anyexp ~ insurance + povcat, logexp ~ insurance,
                  data = meps, index = c("id", "year"),
                  model = "within", boot = 49, seed = 1))
#> 
#> Call:
#> panselect(selection = anyexp ~ insurance + povcat, outcome = logexp ~

#>     boot = 49, seed = 1)

# self-rated health: random effects ordered probit
summary(panglm(health ~ nchronic + I(age / 10) + povcat, data = meps,
               index = c("id", "year"), family = "oprobit",
               model = "random"))
